item.title: UEL: Juventus denied at the death, Sunderland make point in Poland
item.description: Bayer Leverkusen made it three straight wins in the Europa League with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday’s third matchday. The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium’s Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games. Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late ‘winner’ ruled out for a marginal offside. Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead. Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi’s 88th minute strike. Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland. The Blacks Cats took a second-half lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win. With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris’ men. In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor’s 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts. item.title: Tinubu appoints Yusuf Bichi chairman of NISS governing board
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appointed Y. M. Bichi, the immediate past Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), as chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS), Abuja. Bichi’s appointment, based on the recommendation of the current DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, takes effect from October 22, 2026, for an initial four-year term. According to a statement by the Director of Coordination and Liaison, NISS, Lilian Omo-Odigwe, the appointment was made in accordance with Section 4 of the National Institute for Security Studies (Establishment) Act, 2019. Bichi succeeds A. A. Gadzama on the governing board. He handed over leadership of the DSS to the incumbent director-general in August 2024. Before his appointment as DSS director-general, Bichi began his career in the Security Division of the Kano State Cabinet Office before his transfer of service in 1984. His appointment brings experience in intelligence, security administration, operational leadership and institutional training to the governance of the institute. item.title: Tinubu Tasks Medical Experts On Brain Drain Solutions In West Africa

He said the trend limits access to essential medical services and increases the workload on available health personnel. According to a statement by presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu spoke on Thursday after being conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja. He urged the College’s leadership to use its forthcoming conference to develop lasting solutions to the challenge. “We are more challenged in Africa than anywhere else; you know, and with the outbreak of Ebola now we’re looking for a preventive action that will eliminate all these problems and infections. So, I wish you the best. As I pledge to behave myself, I will continue to do whatever I can do for this honourable profession,” the President said. Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to comprehensive health sector reforms aimed at making healthcare delivery more accessible, affordable and efficient for Nigerians. item.description: By Henry Umoru Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC ahead of the 2027 elections, Peter Obi has urged political opponents to keep the Pope, Pope Leo XIV and the Catholic Church out of partisan campaigns. item.title: 2027: APC will campaign on achievements, not insults – Gov. Yusuf
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf has promised that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will focus on issues, achievements and plans rather than personal attacks in its campaign ahead of the 2027 general election. Yusuf gave the assurance on Thursday during the inauguration of the APC 2027 presidential and gubernatorial campaign council management team in Kano. He said the party would explain its achievements to voters, present its plans for the future and listen to the needs of the people. “We are going to campaign based on what the APC leaders have done, not campaign full of insults,” the governor said. Yusuf said members of the campaign council were selected based on their capacity to carry out the responsibilities assigned to them. He urged them to work hard to ensure that the APC secured more votes in Kano than in any other state during the 2027 elections. “Kano should garner a lot of votes for President Tinubu. The number of votes the APC gets in Kano should be the highest in the country. This is possible if you go out and campaign as required,” he said. The governor described the council members as representatives of the party who must work towards securing victory for the APC and President Bola Tinubu. “The members of this council are APC soldiers, and I urge you to carry out your responsibilities with commitment and work towards the party’s victory,” Yusuf said. He also urged them not to be intimidated by opposition parties or allow fear to affect their campaign activities, insisting that the APC had established itself in the state. Yusuf appealed to party members and supporters whose names were not included in the initial campaign council list not to feel disappointed, explaining that additional lists and subcommittees would be announced. He called on party members to remain committed and work together to mobilise support for the APC ahead of the 2027 elections. Among the key appointments, Abdullahi Tijjani Muhammad Gwarzo was named Director-General of the campaign council, while Hon. Bala Muhammad Gwagwarwa will serve as First Deputy Director-General. Dr. Yunusa Adamu Dangwani was appointed Deputy Director-General for Kano South, while Dr. Ali Haruna Abubakar Makoda and Senator Abdussalam Abdulkarim Zaura will serve as Deputy Directors-General for Kano North and Kano Central, respectively. Dr. Mariya Mahmoud Bunkure was also named Assistant Director-General for Women Affairs, while Hon. Garba Yusuf Abubakar will serve as Assistant Director-General for Operations, among other appointments. item.title: Stop announcing how much your movie made at the cinema — Filmmaker Biodun Stephen tells colleagues
item.description: Nollywood filmmaker Biodun Stephen has urged colleagues to stop announcing cinema earnings, warning that the practice puts unnecessary pressure on other filmmakers and creates a narrow definition of success in the industry. Stephen made the remarks during Paul & Baaj: In Character podcast, where she argued that publicising box office figures could distract filmmakers from focusing on the quality and impact of their work. “I think that we really should do away with the announcements,” she said. “I feel like this is a distractions and it puts pressure on those other people who… feel as if that is the determine and that’s how you determine my success,” she added. The filmmaker explained that frequent announcements of cinema earnings could make others feel unsuccessful if their projects failed to achieve similar figures. item.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries falls 6.3% — NMDPRA
item.description: — Petrol supply drops 20.6% By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries fell by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August, while petrol supply from domestic refineries also declined amid reduced imports. The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday showed that average daily petrol receipts dropped by 23.4 per cent to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August. The report attributed the decline to lower domestic supply and reduced imports following the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. Between January and September 2026, Nigerian refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude. Domestic crude accounted for 80.4 per cent of total refinery intake during the period, while imported crude contributed 19.6 per cent. The report also showed that Dangote Refinery operated at 105.98 per cent utilisation in September, processing approximately 689,000 barrels of crude oil per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day. The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from the refinery’s inventory, indicating that it processed more crude than it received during the month. On petrol supply, the NMDPRA data showed that domestic refineries supplied an average of 28.5 million litres per day in September, down 20.6 per cent from 35.9 million litres in August. Petrol imports also declined by 30.1 per cent to 10.2 million litres per day from 14.6 million litres. Despite the decline, domestic refineries remained the largest source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts in September, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports. The September average of 38.7 million litres per day was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026. Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres of petrol per day, representing 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent. The NMDPRA reiterated that September’s decline in petrol receipts reflected a 21 per cent drop in domestic supply from August levels and a 30 per cent reduction in imports amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. item.title: DSS secures 7th death sentence as Adamawa court convicts three over kidnap of Catholic priests
item.description: A high Court of Adamawa State, on Thursday, sentenced to death three persons who kidnapped two Catholic priests in February 2025. Delivering judgement, Justice Christopher Mapeo found the three men guilty of criminal conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, conspiracy to commit armed robbery, armed robbery, harboring a kidnapped person and negotiating to receive ransom for the release of Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi and Abraham Sauman. The judge sentenced the three men, Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan and Mikaila Yusuf, to death for kidnapping, armed robbery and other offences.Thursday’s death sentence is the seventh secured by the DSS this year. On 20th May, 2026, Ekiti High Court sentenced two men, Ibrahim Abubakar and Abdullahi Abubakar to death by hanging for kidnapping. About two weeks later, on 3rd June, 2026, a Federal High Court in Abuja sentenced to death by hanging, four men who, in June 2022, massacred scores of worshippers at the St. Francis Catholic church, Owo, Ondo State. The convicts are Idris Abdulmalik Omeiza, Alqasim Idris, Jamiu Abdulmalik and Abdulkareem Idris. item.title: Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye LaLiga president Javier Tebas has been referred to Spain’s sports tribunal over his comparison of Real Madrid’s communication tactics to Nazi propaganda, following the Spanish club’s demand for his resignation. According to Reuters, Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) announced on Thursday that it had referred Tebas to the Administrative Court for Sport (TAD) to determine whether his remarks breached regulations protecting sporting dignity and decorum. The referral concerns comments Tebas made on social media on October 16, criticising Real Madrid’s handling of complaints about refereeing decisions and the club’s television coverage of match officials. Tebas accused Real Madrid of using communication tactics that recalled propaganda methods employed by Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister. Real Madrid subsequently demanded the immediate resignation of the 64-year-old, describing his comparison as unacceptable for someone holding the position of LaLiga president. However, Tebas insisted that he was referring to propaganda techniques rather than Nazi ideology or Real Madrid’s supporters. In its referral, the CSD asked the tribunal to assess whether the remarks could constitute a serious offence under Article 76.4.b of Spain’s 1990 Sports Law, which covers public acts that infringe upon sporting dignity or decorum. Possible sanctions for such offences include warnings, fines or suspension. The controversy followed Tebas’s criticism of Real Madrid’s efforts to challenge the standard of refereeing in Spanish football. The club has repeatedly questioned officiating decisions through its in-house television channel. In a fresh post on X on Thursday, Tebas defended his comments and questioned why Real Madrid’s accusations against Spanish referees had not attracted similar scrutiny under the rules governing sporting dignity. “Defending the competition also requires responding to those who constantly discredit it,” Tebas wrote, adding that he intended to continue exercising that responsibility. He also argued that Real Madrid’s repeated questioning of the integrity of Spanish football could itself be examined under the same rules. The AFP also reports that the CSD emphasised the importance of protecting respect, coexistence and fair play in sport. The tribunal will determine whether the matter warrants disciplinary proceedings. No finding of wrongdoing against Tebas has been announced. item.title: DSS arrests 23-year-old female arms courier in Nasarawa
item.description: — Sule commends security agencies over crackdown on arms trafficking By Edwin Philip LAFIA — Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, has commended the Department of State Services (DSS) for its sustained efforts to clamp down on gun runners and arms traffickers in the state following the arrest of a 23-year-old female suspected arms courier in Keffi. The governor’s commendation was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by his Press Secretary, Ibrahim Addra, who described the arrest of Aisha Mohammed, a resident of Bwari, Federal Capital Territory, as a significant breakthrough. According to the statement, Mohammed was arrested with 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition and three empty magazines. “The suspect, currently in custody, was arrested while in possession of 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition with three empty magazines,” the statement said. It added that other suspected arms couriers arrested between August and September 2026 included Hassan Sani, 40; Abdulkadir Idrissa, 41; and Salihu Garba, 70, also known as Nabayi. The statement said security operatives recovered 678 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, 99 rounds of 7.5mm ammunition and other items from the suspects. It further disclosed that an alleged arms courier, Ismail Lawalli, a native of Zamfara State, was arrested in August along the Keffi-Abuja highway with 1,262 assorted rounds of ammunition. Sule praised DSS personnel and other security agencies in Nasarawa for their dedication and commitment to tackling arms trafficking and other criminal activities. He also commended the collaboration between the security agencies and his administration, pledging continued government support for their operations. The governor assured residents of his administration’s resolve to combat criminality and called on the public to support security agencies in maintaining peace and safety across the state. item.title: Lawal swears in five permanent secretaries
item.description: — Charges appointees to uphold public service rules, financial regulations By Idris Salisu GUSAU — Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has sworn in five new permanent secretaries into the state civil service, charging them to comply with public service rules, financial regulations and other relevant laws. The swearing-in ceremony took place on Thursday at the Grand Chamber of the Government House in Gusau, with the Chief Judge of the state, Justice Kulu Aliyu, administering the oath of office. The new permanent secretaries are Ahmad S. Zamfara, Nasiru Halilu Anka, Mu’azu Jibril Guraguri, Adamu Abdullahi Kanoma and Sani Muhammad Shinkafi. Speaking at the ceremony, Lawal said the appointments reflected confidence in the officers’ experience, abilities and readiness to assume greater responsibilities in the state’s administration. He said permanent secretaries played a critical role in providing administrative leadership, ensuring institutional continuity, advising on policy implementation and maintaining discipline within the civil service. “Becoming permanent secretaries is more than personal advancement: as senior administrative leaders, your decisions and conduct directly affect government performance and the welfare of the people we serve,” the governor said. Lawal said his administration remained committed to strengthening government institutions and improving public administration to support the state’s development agenda. He urged the appointees to ensure that government policies were backed by proper planning, realistic implementation strategies, effective supervision and continuous assessment of results. “Proper planning, realistic implementation strategies, effective supervision and continuous assessment of results must support policies and programmes,” he said. The governor also advised the permanent secretaries to maintain professional relationships with commissioners and other political officeholders, stressing the need for cooperation between political leaders and career civil servants. “Political leaders set policy; career civil servants provide the institutional knowledge, technical advice, and administrative capacity to implement it. These roles complement each other, and the effectiveness of the government depends on mutual respect,” he said. Lawal said the civil service remained central to translating government decisions into tangible results, particularly in the delivery of essential services and the implementation of reforms aimed at meeting the needs and aspirations of Zamfara residents. He urged the new permanent secretaries to approach their assignments with discipline, professionalism and a clear understanding of the administration’s priorities. item.title: Makinde Rallies South-West To Lead Nigeria’s Rebirth
item.description: Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has urged the Southwest to lead Nigeria’s national rebirth, calling on the region to reject entitlement, nepotism and “turn-by-turn” politics. Makinde made the call on Thursday at the APM Southwest Town Hall held at the Ondo State International Conference Centre, The Dome, in Akure, where he presented his Reset Nigeria agenda as a pathway to national renewal. He described the Southwest as a historic vanguard of Nigeria’s progress, arguing that the region must once again take the lead in shaping the country’s political and economic future. The governor dismissed suggestions that the Southwest should not produce another presidential candidate because the region currently holds the presidency. He cited the 1999 presidential election, when former President Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae contested for the country’s highest office without controversy. Makinde at the APM South West Town Hall Meeting in Akure on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Facebook/Seyi Makinde. According to him, leadership should be determined by competence, energy and readiness to serve, rather than claims of entitlement to political office. item.title: NEC Endorses 90-Day Economic Plan To Ease Cost Of Living For Nigerians
item.description: The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate the gains of President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, with a focus on reducing the cost of living and improving food affordability. The plan also prioritises attracting investment, removing bottlenecks to economic activities and accelerating the completion of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians. According to a statement by Stanley Nkwocha, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications in the Office of the Vice President, the endorsement followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, at NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually on Thursday and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima. The five priority areas identified in the plan are food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. 161st NEC meeting on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting on the utilisation of proceeds from fuel subsidy removal. Presenting the economic outlook, Oyedele expressed optimism about progress under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery. He identified reducing headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions. The presentation also highlighted the need to translate macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment. Addressing Council members, Shettima said that although President Tinubu’s economic reforms were designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels must ensure that the objectives translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. The presentation also highlighted the need to translate macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment. It needs disagreement, scrutiny and the freedom to challenge those who govern. But disagreement should not become permission to dehumanise. Political opponents are not enemies of the nation. “Critics are not automatically traitors. Supporters are not exempt from the duty to tell the truth. In a tense season, words can become fuel. “A false allegation can travel through a community before the person accused has a chance to respond. A divisive appeal to ethnicity or religion can turn a neighbour into a suspect. And a manipulated video or an invented quotation can harden opinions before the facts are known,” he added. Leadership Matters Stressing the importance of leadership, the CEO explained that political leaders and public figures have the reach to calm a moment or inflame it. “They can reject language that invites violence, correct claims made by their own supporters, and remind people that the contest for office must not destroy the country we all share,” he added. On the economy, Momoh said that the credibility of any economic story “depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives”. According to him, the economy also has its own powerful narrative because people feel it at the kitchen table. “Families weigh the cost of food, transport, rent, school fees, power and healthcare. A promising economic indicator matters, but citizens want to know whether their lives are becoming more manageable,” he said. “The World Bank reported that Nigeria’s real GDP grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026. The Central Bank’s figures showed year-on-year headline inflation easing to 14.63 per cent in September from 15.39 per cent in August. “These are positive movements. But when inflation falls, prices may still be rising, only at a slower pace. It does not mean that the cost of living has returned to what families could afford before.” Speaking further, the media chief stated, “This distinction matters for public communication. If an official says that inflation has eased, and a family hears that food is still more expensive, the family is not being unreasonable. The two statements can both be true. Good leadership explains the difference and keeps working on the effect people actually feel. “Growth must mean more than a number. It must become decent jobs, dependable public services, wages that can support a household, opportunity for young people, and confidence that the effort to build a life is worthwhile. The credibility of any economic story depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives.” Promoting Security Momoh also emphasised the need for intelligence, training, coordination, and public support to strengthen security agencies in the country. “Security is an even more immediate measure. Across the country, communities face insurgent violence, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflict, farmer–pastoralist tensions and other threats. In Adamawa and the wider North-East, insecurity has disrupted homes, farming, education, livelihoods and family life,” he said. “We must speak of these realities with care. Behind every statistic is a person: a child who cannot attend school, a farmer afraid to return to a field, a family forced from its home, a community unable to reach a clinic. Their experience must not be reduced to a talking point in a political argument. “Our security agencies need intelligence, equipment, training, coordination and public support.” The chief executive further stated that communities need protection and a reason to trust that reports will be heard. Justice must follow crime, and prevention must accompany response. “A government’s account of security will be judged by whether people can live, work, travel, learn and sleep without fear,” said Momoh. “These are not easy stories to tell. But a good national narrative does not hide difficult truths. It gives them names, identifies responsibility, reports what is being done, and allows citizens to see whether the response is working.” On governance, he urged political leaders to match words with action for the benefit of the citizens “Every government tells a story about its purpose. It may speak of renewal, reform, development, security or opportunity. But the public does not assess that story by the words alone. People compare it with their lived experience,” he stated. “When leaders promise a road, citizens watch to see whether it is built. When government promises relief, people ask whether it reaches those who need it. When officials announce a reform, families want to understand why it is necessary, what it will cost them, what support is available, and what success will look like. “Good communication therefore begins with the quality of the decision. If a policy has not been thought through, if its impact has not been understood, or if those who carry its cost have not been heard, communication cannot repair the weakness. It may postpone the reckoning, but it will not remove it.” “Leadership must make room for honest advice before decisions are announced. It must ask: who will benefit? Who may be harmed? What evidence supports this choice? What will we do if the expected result does not come? How will we explain the trade-offs without talking down to the public? “The public also needs to see that leaders accept responsibility. If a project is delayed, say why and give a credible timeline. If a service fails, acknowledge it and explain how the failure will be addressed. If a claim was wrong, by all means correct it. A leader’s willingness to repair a mistake can strengthen trust more than pretending the mistake never happened,” he added. Mohom commended Governor Fintiri for the achievements recorded in Adamawa. “I would like to acknowledge the work your administration is doing to transform Adamawa. Investment in roads and urban renewal, public buildings, schools and healthcare facilities is changing the state’s landscape and strengthening access to public services,” he said. “These efforts deserve recognition, and the people of Adamawa deserve a clear account of what has been completed, what is under way and what remains to be done.” He described Epelle as one who understood that communication goes beyond sending out information and encompasses the work of building understanding and confidence between an institution and the people it serves.
